# Flipkart fixtures

Made-up Flipkart orders only: made-up names, order IDs and links. Never a real file, and nothing copied from one. Write the file again with `node test/fixtures/flipkart/make-flipkart.mjs`. The only real pages here are `product-page.html`, `reviews-page-1.html` and `reviews-page-2.html` (below), with every reviewer's name made up.

- `flipkart-orders.xlsx`: three tabs, "Amazon", "Flipkart" and "Notes". Only "Flipkart" is read.
  - Row 1 holds the column names: Order ID, Order Date, Product, Amount, Reviewer Name, Order Screenshot, Delivery Screenshot, Review Link, Email ID, Review Screenshot.
  - Made-up order IDs as Flipkart writes them: OD and 18 digits (`OD100000000000000002`).
  - A real Excel date and a date written as words (`21-07-2026`); amounts as numbers (one with paise, `349.5`) and as words (`₹499`).
  - Links behind their words: `Screenshot` (row 2), links behind themselves (row 2), and `Open review` put there by a HYPERLINK formula (row 4).
  - Links written in the words: a link alone (row 3), two links in one cell (row 4), and a link inside a sentence (row 6).
  - A cell with two lines (row 4), empty cells (row 6), and an empty row 5.
  - Pictures placed inside cells (row 3, Order Screenshot and Review Screenshot), a picture over a cell (row 3, Delivery Screenshot), and a row with only a picture in it (row 7).
  - A row with a review screenshot and no review link (row 6).
- `zip-tools.mjs`: writes a zip with Node's own zlib, puts pictures inside cells the way Excel stores them, and draws a tiny made-up picture.
- `product-page.html`: one real Flipkart product page (Renee Pink Therapy Collagen Night Wrapping Face Mask, product ID FCPHEW7AM9C7RU24, item ID itm50a9094e8e73a), opened once on 2026-10-12 with the user's leave, signed out, in a fresh Chrome profile that let only Flipkart's own addresses load, and saved as Chrome showed it. Changed before it was saved here: every script left out except its JSON-LD (what the page tells search engines: the name, the brand, the product ID, the stars and the counts); the links to Flipkart's page code and styles left out (the canonical link kept); every reviewer's name swapped for a made-up one ("Test Reviewer One" to "Test Reviewer Six"; "Flipkart Customer" is Flipkart's own word and stays), in the page and in its JSON-LD; the reviewers' photos left out, and the photos' file names too; and one word in Flipkart's top menu changed, because this project bans it. The page shows 4.2 stars from 1,355 ratings, and its JSON-LD says 47 reviews.
- `reviews-page-1.html` and `reviews-page-2.html`: the first two pages of that product's reviews, newest first (`sortOrder=MOST_RECENT`, ten reviews each), opened once each on 2026-10-12 with the user's leave, signed out, at least 3 seconds apart, in a fresh Chrome profile that let only Flipkart's own addresses load and no other page open; no login box showed. Saved as Chrome showed each page once it had loaded, with the page's own data from the page as Flipkart sent it (its `window.__INITIAL_STATE__`), cut down to its reviews: each one's own ID, stars, title, text, date words, city and whether it is a certified purchase. Changed before they were saved here: every other script left out; the links to Flipkart's page code and styles left out; every reviewer's name swapped for a made-up one ("Test Reviewer One" to "Test Reviewer Fourteen"; "Flipkart Customer" stays), in the page and in its data; the reviewers' photos and their file names left out; and the same word in the top menu changed. The pages show "User reviews sorted by" with "Most Helpful" next to it, yet their reviews go from the newest (14 days ago) to the oldest (6 months ago).
- `reviews-page-3.html` (made up: a third page of older reviews, with none of the page's own data), `reviews-read-more.html` (made up: a review cut short with "Read more", which shows the whole text), `reviews-login-box.html` (made up: reviews under a login box like Flipkart's, taken away by its close button; it counts any key pressed) and `reviews-none.html` (made up: a product with no reviews).
- `robot-check-page.html`, `blocked-page.html` (served as refused, 403), `error-page.html` (served as an error, 500), `not-found-page.html` (served as not found, 404) and `search-page.html` (not a product's page): made up, since Flipkart showed none of these. The robot check and the block are written the way such pages usually look.
- `fake-flipkart.mjs`: answers the Live Flipkart Browser in the tests with these pages, inside the test's own hidden Chrome, so nothing reaches Flipkart. Every other address, and every picture, script or other part a page asks for, is refused. No redirects.
- `made-up-files.mjs`: makes, on the spot, a made-up PDF with a coloured box on each page (to be drawn into one picture with the Mac's own tools) and a large picture of made-up dots (to be made smaller). The pretend Google Drive in the screenshot tests answers with these and with the tiny pictures from `zip-tools.mjs`.
